news.title: Lionel Messi subjected to World Cup murder threat, US authorities reveal
news.lede: Spanish newspaper Marca has disclosed details from a chilling American police report, which lists all the security threats faced by the FBI and the International Police Cooperation Center (IPCC) this summer. According to the news outlet, Argentina superstar Messi received more threats than any other player throughout the tournament. The risk extended to his national teammates, with the report revealing one plot during their final group game against Jordan. One man is said to have rung up Dallas Airport and warned that he and two others would storm the stadium with "homemade bombs and an AR-15 [rifle]."

news.title: Is football AI-proof? Why tech investors wanted a slice of the World Cup
news.lede: Fifa has been forced to U-turn on plans to sell off a slice of the World Cup after fierce opposition, with threats of future boycotts and calls for the governing body's president, Gianni Infantino, to quit. But why were a group of tech investors interested in the World Cup in the first place, and are similar proposals in the future inevitable? In a world in which AI could upend human recreation and pastimes, executives at Thrive Eternal, a spin-off of venture capital firm Thrive Capital, saw an opportunity to lead a group of investors to place cash in the biggest sporting competition on the planet. The football World Cup was seen as the latest in a new strategy from firm, which believes that sport will not only survive the AI revolution, but grow in value.

news.title: Scotland closing in on new head coach
news.lede: Steve Clarke stepped down after Scotland's World Cup campaign this summer. The Scottish FA is closing in on the appointment of a new head coach to succeed Steve Clarke. Clarke, who had signed a new four-year deal in May, resigned following Scotland's group-stage exit at the World Cup this summer, ending his seven-year tenure. Scotland return to action in the Nations League with a four-game block of fixtures, which begins away to Slovenia on 26 September.

news.title: Infantino allies rally as Norway FA demands FIFA president’s resignation
news.lede: Embattled FIFA president Gianni Infantino visiting a sports complex in Cali, Colombia, on Aug 7. ZURICH – Football appeared to be headed for a prolonged stand-off on Aug 7 as allies of FIFA president Gianni Infantino rallied behind him while Norway demanded his resignation after several European associations withdrew their support. Confederations and national associations continued to choose sides a week after Infantino abandoned his proposal to raise about US$4.2 billion (S$5.4 billion) by selling off a stake in the commercial rights of the World Cup and other tournaments. Norwegian Football Federation president Lise Klaveness said Infantino no longer had the confidence of the football community, saying the sport needed to move beyond Game Of Thrones power struggles and focus on real governance reform.

news.title: Book Review – Uruguay: Football’s First Global Power 1918-1930
news.lede: 30th July 1930: Jules Rimet, president of FIFA (Federation Internationale de Football), presents the first World Cup trophy (the Jules Rimet Trophy) to Dr Paul Jude, the president of the Uruguayan Football Association, after Uruguay beat Argentina 4-2 in the first ever World Cup final in Montevideo, Uruguay. (Photo by Keystone/Getty Images). As increased popularity and professionalism saw football start to outgrow the Olympic Games in the 1920s, momentum gathered for the sport to have a dedicated competition of it own. Football was about to become the global game, and at the centre of it was Uruguay, a tiny, little-known South American nation.

news.title: Messi was target of bomb threats during World Cup, leaked FBI files reveal
news.lede: A portion of the classified reports has been published by the investigative crime channel of Spain-based media outlet Prensa Ibérica. The documents, prepared jointly by the FBI and the International Police Cooperation Centre (IPCC), detail a series of security incidents involving footballers, coaches and match officials before and during the tournament. Among the players, Messi appears to have faced the most serious threats. One of the most alarming incidents occurred on the day of Argentina’s match against Jordan.
